newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: U.S. AGENCY, BOTSWANA UNITE FOR DEVELOPMENT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. AGENCY, BOTSWANA UNITE FOR DEVELOPMENT.

text.p: The U.S. government-based African Development Foundation (ADF) and the Botswana government united on Wednesday to help fund grassroots development.
The ADF is donating $2.3 million, which will be matched by the government of President Ketumile Masire.
A memorandum of understanding signed on Wednesday said the partnership would help to further reduce poverty and promote sustainable development in the southern African country.
"The agreement symbolises how governments are becoming aware of the need for community-based development," ADF Vice President Nate Fields said.
Fields added the agreement was breaking new ground in the relationship between the AFD and African countries, in that it was the first time such a partnership deal had been signed.

"Before we have acted entirely on our own. Working together with the people of Botswana at grassroots level in participatory development effort is a new innovation, a model of African ownership and self-reliance," he said.
Under the agreement, rural communities will identify needs which will be evaluated by Batswana consultants and officials of ADF and if if accepted, be funded by the programme.
